full_text_zh:
[P1] 连环计

[P2] 三国时期，曹操率领八十万大军，来到了长江北岸。他要渡过长江，攻打对岸的东吴。曹操想，东吴大都督周瑜有勇有谋，如果能劝他投降，打下东吴不是轻而易举吗？可是，派谁去劝降呢？这时候，他的谋士蒋干说："主公，周瑜是我的同窗，我愿凭三寸不烂之舌，劝他投降主公！"

[P3] 于是，曹操派出一艘小船，把蒋干送去了东吴。周瑜摆酒设宴，热情地招待了蒋干。宴席上，蒋干劝周瑜投降，周瑜却不接话。蒋干便假装醉酒，晚上睡在了周瑜的房间里。夜里，周瑜的鼾声像打雷一样。蒋干趁他熟睡，翻看书桌，竟然发现了一封密信：大都督，等我们找个机会，杀掉曹操，就来投奔您。

[P4] 蒋干一看落款，大吃一惊，写信的人竟然是曹操的两名水军将领。他心里急得像火烧，再也睡不着了。天刚放亮，他就急匆匆地回了曹营。见到曹操，蒋干马上向他禀告了密信的内容。曹操立刻下令，把两名水军将领斩首。可是，这样一来，曹军中就没有擅长水战的将领了。

[P5] 周瑜听说后，哈哈大笑起来。原来，那封信是周瑜伪造的。周瑜故意让蒋干看到假信，借机除掉了曹操最厉害的两名水军将领。这一计成功了！只是，光除掉水军将领，还不能让曹操停止进攻，还是得想办法打败他呀！

[P6] 曹军的几百艘战船，密密麻麻地停靠在长江北岸。周瑜手下的老将黄盖说：‘我们可以用火攻，烧掉曹操的战船。他没船不能渡江，还怎么进攻东吴呢？’可是，谁能靠近曹军的战船，点燃这把火呢？曹操有那么多艘船，又怎么能一次都烧光呢！
怎么点燃这把火呢？

[P7] 黄盖心生一计，说："末将愿意假装向曹操投降，点燃这把火。" 周瑜的谋士庞统也胸有成竹地一笑："我愿意深入曹营，劝说曹操，让他把船连起来。这样，一次就能把他的船烧个干净！"

[P8] 第二天，周瑜召集将领们开会。他命令大家各领三个月的粮草，做好攻打曹军的准备。黄盖却打断周瑜的话，抢着说：‘不要说三个月，就是领三十个月的粮草，我们也赢不了曹操。如果这个月内不能打败曹军，大家干脆都投降吧！’

[P9] 真是长他人志气，灭自己威风。周瑜勃然大怒，立刻下令将黄盖拖出去，重打一百军棍。行刑的士兵剥光黄盖的衣服，狠狠地打了起来。“啪——啪——啪——”才五十军棍，就打得黄盖背上鲜血直流，昏死过去。黄盖又恨又气，在病床上给曹操写了一封信，要投降于他。

[P10] 曹操收到信后，心里琢磨不定，便又派蒋干去东吴军中打探消息。周瑜见了蒋干，板着脸说："上次你偷看我的密信，误了我的大事。今天再也不能留你了。"说完，他叫来士兵，把蒋干送进了山中的一座小庙里。

[P11] 蒋干心中又烦又闷，便在山间闲逛。忽然，他听到一间茅屋中传出了一阵阵读书声。读书人是谁呢？他就是三国时期大名鼎鼎的凤雏先生庞统。蒋干和庞统见面后，心里乐开了花。他想到曹操正在四处招揽人才，便邀请庞统一起去投奔曹操。趁看守的士兵不注意，他们连夜下山，乘船回了曹营。

[P12] 听说名士庞统来投靠，曹操亲自出来迎接，还带他参观了自己的战船。曹操苦恼地说："我军士兵是北方人，都有晕船的毛病，受不了颠簸，一上船就呕吐生病。唉，这一仗难打呀！"庞统捋着胡子，笑着说："我有一计，或许可行。您把大小战船并在一起，用铁环锁住，铺上宽阔的木板。这样，战船就像平地一样平稳，风浪再大也不用怕了。"

[P13] 曹操听后，连忙派人打造铁环，像庞统说的那样，把船锁在了一起。果然，船稳当多了。人走上去，就像在平地上一样，还可以在上面跑马呢！
现在，解决了士兵晕船的大难题，曹操高兴极了。他又得到密报——黄盖是真的要投降。曹操得意地等着黄盖来降，心里盘算着这回一定能一举打败东吴。

[P14] 到了约定的日子，黄盖准备了二十艘大船，后面用绳子拴着小船。大船上装满芦苇和干柴，浇上鱼油，铺好引火用的硫黄、火硝，用青布盖住。等到了晚上，趁着呼呼的东南风，船队飞一般地向江北岸驶去。等到离曹军战船几百米的水面上，黄盖和士兵们跳上小船，大刀一挥，砍断绳子，点燃了大船。

[P15] 借着风的威力，大船像火箭一样，射向了曹军的战船。曹军的战船被铁环锁在一起，逃不能逃，顿时烧成了一片火海。
火苗蹿到岸上，岸边曹军的兵营也烧了起来，哭喊声响成一片。这时候，周瑜带着兵马打了过来，曹操见手下的兵将丢盔弃甲，无心应战，只得带着他们逃跑了。

[P16] 周瑜先用反间计，除掉了曹操的水军将领；然后用庞统的锁船计，让曹操将战船紧紧地锁在一起；最后使出苦肉计，让黄盖向曹操诈降，火烧了曹营。在这场对局中，周瑜的三计一环套一环，任何一计失败，都不能获胜。像这样多计并用，给敌人设下一个又一个圈套的计策，就叫“连环计”。
full_text_en:
[P1] Chain Strategy

[P2] In the Three Kingdoms period, Cao Cao led an army of 800,000 troops to the northern bank of the Yangtze River. He planned to cross the river and attack the Eastern Wu across the water. Cao Cao thought, 'The Eastern Wu's Grand Commander Zhou Yu is brave and wise. If we could persuade him to surrender, wouldn't conquering Eastern Wu be easy? But who should we send to persuade him?' At this moment, his strategist Jiang Gan said, 'My lord, Zhou Yu was my classmate. I am willing to use my eloquence to persuade him to surrender to you!'

[P3] Then, Cao Cao sent a small boat to carry Jiang Gan to Eastern Wu. Zhou Yu held a banquet and warmly entertained Jiang Gan. At the feast, Jiang Gan tried to persuade Zhou Yu to surrender, but Zhou Yu remained silent. Jiang Gan then pretended to be drunk and slept in Zhou Yu's room that night. In the night, Zhou Yu's snoring sounded like thunder. Taking advantage of his deep sleep, Jiang Gan searched the desk and discovered a secret letter: 'Grand Commander, when we find an opportunity, we will kill Cao Cao and come to surrender to you.'

[P4] Jiang Gan looked at the signature and was greatly shocked — the letter was from two of Cao Cao's naval commanders. His heart raced like fire; he couldn't sleep anymore. As soon as dawn broke, he hurried back to Cao Cao's camp. Upon seeing Cao Cao, Jiang Gan immediately reported the contents of the secret letter. Cao Cao immediately ordered the two naval commanders to be executed. However, as a result, Cao Cao's army no longer had any generals skilled in naval warfare.

[P5] Zhou Yu heard this and burst out laughing. It turned out the letter was forged by Zhou Yu. Zhou Yu deliberately let Jiang Gan see the fake letter, using the opportunity to eliminate Cao Cao's two most capable naval commanders. The plan had succeeded! However, merely removing the naval commanders was not enough to stop Cao Cao's advance; they still needed to find a way to defeat him!

[P6] Cao Cao's hundreds of warships were tightly packed along the northern bank of the Yangtze River. Huang Gai, an old general under Zhou Yu, said: 'We can use fire attack to burn Cao Cao's ships. Without boats, he can't cross the river—how can he attack Wu then?' But who could get close to Cao Cao's warships and light the fire? Cao Cao has so many ships—how could we possibly burn them all at once?
How can we light this fire?

[P7] Huang Gai thought of a plan and said, "I am willing to pretend to surrender to Cao Cao and set this fire." Zhou Yu's strategist Pang Tong smiled confidently, "I am willing to go deep into Cao's camp, persuade Cao Cao to link his ships together. This way, we can burn all his ships at once!"

[P8] The next day, Zhou Yu called a meeting with his generals. He ordered everyone to take three months' worth of provisions to prepare for attacking Cao Cao's army. Huang Gai, however, interrupted Zhou Yu, exclaiming: 'Don't even talk about three months— even if we take provisions for thirty months, we still can't defeat Cao Cao. If we can't defeat his army within this month, let's just surrender!'

[P9] This is truly boosting others' morale while undermining our own. Zhou Yu became furious and immediately ordered Huang Gai to be dragged out and beaten with one hundred military rods. The executioners stripped Huang Gai naked and began beating him fiercely. "Smack—smack—smack—" After only fifty rods, Huang Gai's back was covered in blood and he fainted. Filled with hatred and anger, Huang Gai wrote a letter to Cao Cao from his sickbed, offering to surrender.

[P10] Cao Cao received the letter and was deeply troubled, so he sent Jiang Gan again to spy on the Eastern Wu army. Zhou Yu saw Jiang Gan and said sternly, "Last time you secretly read my confidential letter and ruined my plan. I can't keep you here any longer." Then he called his soldiers and sent Jiang Gan to a small temple in the mountains.

[P11] Jiang Gan felt troubled and restless, so he wandered through the mountains. Suddenly, he heard the sound of reading coming from a thatched hut. Who was the reader? It was Pang Tong, the famous 'Fengchu' of the Three Kingdoms period. After meeting Pang Tong, Jiang Gan was overjoyed. He thought of Cao Cao's ongoing search for talented people, and invited Pang Tong to join him in defecting to Cao Cao's camp. Taking advantage of the guards' inattention, they secretly descended the mountain and sailed back to Cao Cao's camp.

[P12] Hearing that the famous scholar Pang Tong had come to join him, Cao Cao personally came out to welcome him and took him to tour his warships. Cao Cao worriedly said, "My soldiers are from the north; they all suffer from seasickness, can't stand the rocking, and get sick as soon as they board a ship. Alas, this battle will be hard to win!" Pang Tong, stroking his beard, smiled and said, "I have a plan, perhaps it will work. You can link the large and small warships together, lock them with iron rings, and lay wide wooden planks on top. This way, the warships will be as stable as flat ground, and even the biggest waves won't be a problem."

[P13] Cao Cao, upon hearing this, immediately sent people to forge iron rings and, as Pang Tong suggested, locked the ships together. Indeed, the ships became much more stable. People could walk on them as if on flat ground, and even ride horses on top!
Now, having solved the major problem of soldiers getting seasick, Cao Cao was overjoyed. He also received a secret report — Huang Gai was truly planning to surrender. Cao Cao waited proudly for Huang Gai to come over, calculating in his mind that this time he would surely defeat Eastern Wu in one fell swoop.

[P14] On the agreed-upon day, Huang Gai prepared twenty large ships, each tethered to a small boat behind. The large ships were loaded with reeds and dry firewood, doused with fish oil, and covered with sulfur, saltpeter, and green cloth. At night, taking advantage of the strong southeast wind, the fleet sped toward the northern bank of the river. When they were hundreds of meters away from Cao Cao's fleet, Huang Gai and his soldiers jumped onto the small boats, swung their swords, cut the ropes, and set the large ships ablaze.

[P15] With the power of the wind, the large ships shot like rockets toward Cao Cao's fleet. Cao Cao's ships, chained together with iron rings, could not escape and instantly turned into a sea of fire.
Flames spread to the shore, setting Cao Cao's camps ablaze, and cries of panic echoed everywhere. At that moment, Zhou Yu led his troops in attack. Seeing his soldiers discard their armor and weapons and lose heart, Cao Cao had no choice but to flee with them.

[P16] Zhou Yu first used the counterintelligence plot to eliminate Cao Cao's naval commander; then used Pang Tong's ship-linking strategy to have Cao Cao chain his warships tightly together; finally, he employed the bitter meat plot, making Huang Gai pretend to surrender to Cao Cao and set fire to Cao's camp. In this confrontation, Zhou Yu's three strategies were interlocked — if any one failed, victory was impossible. Such a strategy, using multiple plans in succession to set one trap after another for the enemy, is called the 'Chain Strategy'.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页标题为“连环计”，画面中一位古代人物正坐着阅读卷轴，面前摆放着小桌和果盘，场景简洁，暗示故事即将展开。
[P2] 本页讲述了三国时期曹操率军抵达长江北岸，欲攻打东吴，谋士蒋干自荐去劝降周瑜的故事。
[P3] 本页描绘了蒋干被曹操派往东吴，周瑜设宴款待他，蒋干假装醉酒留宿周瑜房间，并趁其熟睡时偷看书桌，发现一封密信，信中内容是东吴将领欲杀曹操后投奔周瑜。
[P4] 蒋干发现密信后连夜返回曹营，向曹操禀报内容，曹操下令斩杀两名水军将领，导致曹军失去擅长水战的将领。
[P5] 周瑜得知蒋干带回密信后大笑，揭示信件是伪造的，借机除掉了曹操的两名水军将领，但意识到还需进一步计策才能击败曹操。
[P6] 周瑜的部将黄盖提出用火攻烧毁曹军战船，但众人担忧无法靠近敌船并一次性烧毁所有战船，画面中一名将领正思考如何点燃火把。
[P7] 黄盖提出假装投降曹操以实施火攻，庞统则建议让曹操将战船连在一起，以便一次性烧毁，两人共同为火攻计策出谋划策。
[P8] 周瑜召集将领开会，命令大家准备三个月粮草以攻打曹军，但黄盖打断并直言若一个月内无法取胜便应投降，表现出对战局的悲观情绪。
[P9] 周瑜因黄盖提出投降建议而大怒，下令将其重打一百军棍，黄盖被打至昏死，后在病床上写信给曹操表示投降。
[P10] 曹操因收到密信后心神不宁，再次派蒋干去东吴探听消息。周瑜见到蒋干后，因他上次偷看密信而大怒，将其送入山中一座小庙。
[P11] 蒋干在山中闲逛时，遇见了隐居的庞统，两人一见如故。蒋干邀请庞统一同投奔曹操，趁夜乘船返回曹营。
[P12] 庞统向曹操献计，建议将战船用铁环连接并铺上木板，以解决北方士兵晕船的问题，使战船在风浪中保持平稳。
[P13] 曹操采纳庞统的建议，用铁环将战船连在一起，解决了士兵晕船的问题，并得知黄盖将投降，因此信心大增，认为可以一举击败东吴。
[P14] 黄盖率领装满易燃物的大船，在东南风的助力下驶向曹军水寨，待接近后砍断绳索并点燃大船，实施火攻。
[P15] 黄盖的火船借风势冲向曹军战船，因战船被铁链相连无法逃脱，瞬间化为火海，火势蔓延至岸上兵营，周瑜趁机率军进攻，曹操兵败溃逃。
[P16] 本页总结了周瑜在赤壁之战中使用的三计：反间计、锁船计和苦肉计，指出这些计策环环相扣，共同构成了‘连环计’，最终导致曹操兵败。
